title: Superlinear Wire Lower Bounds for Gates of Fan-In N1-δ
content: For every \(\delta>0\), a language in ENP needs more than \(c(\delta)N\sqrt{\log N}\) wires in circuits of any depth on \(N\) inputs whose gates are arbitrary Boolean functions of at most \(N^{1-\delta}\) inputs, or threshold, exact, modular or symmetric gates of any fan-in with weights of at most \(N^{1-\delta}\) bits. The proof extends the tensor-network contraction theorem of OpenAI from degree \(s^{9/10}\) to degree \(s^{1-\delta}\) and counts the satisfying inputs of such circuits in time \(2^{O(s/\sqrt{\log s})}\). The \(\mathrm{P}\) versus \(\mathrm{NP}\) problem remains open, and we show where the method stops.
